newsitem.title: USA: CME adopts cash settlement in 13-week bill futures.
newsitem.headline: CME adopts cash settlement in 13-week bill futures.

text.p: The Chicago Mercantile Exchange said Thursday it adopted cash-settlement for its 13-week U.S. Treasury bill futures and futures-options, effective today.
The Commodity Futures Trading Commission approved the switch to cash settlement from physical delivery June 4.
CME initially will list December 1997 and March 1998 T-bill contract months of the March quarterly cycle.

It also said it will add the first two serial contract months not in the March cycle - in this case, October and November 1997 - when it offers the corresponding serial Eurodollar contracts for trading.

The amended T-bill futures will settle to the weighted average discount rate of the T-bill auction that aligns with the IMM settlement dates of the Eurodollar and LIBOR futures and futures-options contracts, CME added.
The CFTC also approved CME's plan for all-or-none (AON) trading in T-bill futures, with a 100-contract minimum threshold.
Under CME's AON program, customers specify that an order either be filled in the trading pit at a single specified price or not be filled at all.
